tasks.short: Handle routine correspondence, calls, document preparation, office equipment and confidential materials.

steps.what: Open, sort and route incoming correspondence.
Answer calls, establish the caller's need and handle sensitive conversations.
Record call messages and forward them to the responsible colleague.
Type, format and check routine documents from instructions and templates.

loop.input: Document instructions, approved template and supplied facts.
loop.output: Draft document with unsupported or missing facts marked.
loop.check: Validate required fields and supplied facts; the file clerk checks wording before release.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; incomplete or failed checks return to manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill fixed fields, but varied prose instructions sometimes require a bounded drafting step.

steps.what: Scan, copy or print materials and check page completeness.
Place confidential originals in restricted storage and secure work areas.

tasks.design: Configure intake queues, routing rules and short message forms in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to the {DOCS}. Generate routine documents from approved templates, using a bounded drafting loop only for prose instructions and clerk approval before release. Digital delivery reduces printing; physical handling and sensitive calls remain with the clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mixed paper and digital work, inconsistent templates and fragmented routing made small improvements costly to assemble.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, templates and routing features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting them; drafting models can handle a narrow prose step.
tasks.still_hard: Opening envelopes, handling originals and securing rooms remain physical work. Confidential content needs appropriate GDPR controls; any recording or employee monitoring requires separate assessment under EU law and national rules.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk recognises distress, ambiguous requests and situations where a confidential document should not enter the routine queue.

ambition.what: Template-based document preparation for shift supervisors.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer formatting jobs and message transfers. The clerk can resolve routine routing exceptions within an agreed directory, while records owners retain disclosure authority.

reach.task: Prepare routine correspondence from approved templates.
reach.learn: Template field design, plain-language checking and document version control.

evidence.claim: Forms, templates and routing rules can reduce routine office administration; physical handling remains.
TOPdesk Robin can answer from a knowledge base or create a pre-filled request, supporting the intake pattern.
Bounded drafting from supplied facts is feasible, but the digest provides no measured file-clerk case.

assumptions: This illustrative mid-size European office still handles paper correspondence and confidential originals.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
The varied activities are recurring work branches, rather than one sequence followed for every item.
Call messages use short structured entry; recording and transcription are outside the design.
Build ranges are working-day estimates; consultation under national rules may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Paper volumes, call mix and the proportion of documents already generated from templates.
Available routing, scanning and template features in the existing systems.
Permitted processing locations and access arrangements for confidential documents.
Whether employee consultation is required for the proposed changes under national rules.
research_questions: Which document types can use fixed templates without a model?
How reliably can supplied facts and missing fields be checked before draft release?
Which paper copies can be replaced by approved digital delivery?
new_work: Check generated prose and resolve incomplete instructions.
Handle failed scans and misrouted items.
Periodically verify access settings on generated documents.

tasks.short: Track filed and withdrawn materials, reconcile movements and produce inventory reports.

steps.what: Record item identifiers, locations and borrowers on movement slips.
Transcribe movement slips into the electronic file register.
Compare register exports with slips and track overdue or unmatched movements.
Contact borrowers, investigate discrepancies and confirm corrections.
Generate and circulate filing, withdrawal and overdue-item reports.

tasks.design: Configure a movement register in the {DOCS}, capturing item and borrower identifiers at handover so paper slips and transcription disappear. A deterministic reconciliation job flags overdue items and conflicting movements, while scheduled reports show inventory and recovery actions. The clerk investigates disputed movements and confirms corrections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical handovers were separate from the electronic register, and identifiers were not consistently captured at source.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records features and identifier scanning may cover the register. Small deterministic connectors and reports are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding; no model is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded handovers, missing labels and disputed custody cannot be solved from register data alone. Borrower logs need proportionate access and retention under GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk establishes what actually happened when the physical item and the register disagree.

ambition.what: Weekly recovery priorities for overdue originals.

tasks.altitude: Routine logging and report preparation shrink substantially. The clerk gains discretion to prioritise recovery follow-up within agreed deadlines; write-offs and retention decisions remain with records owners.

reach.task: Prioritise document-recovery work and identify recurring custody failures.
reach.learn: Exception ageing, custody controls and service reporting.

evidence.claim: Identifier capture, movement validation and scheduled inventory reports are deterministic records functions.
AFAS self-service changes flow into payroll, illustrating capture once and reuse across systems, rather than physical-file tracking.
The digest contains no documented file-register case supporting a specific saving.

assumptions: The current office uses paper movement slips followed by an electronic register; this is one common mixed arrangement.
Direct capture replaces duplicate transcription, but scanning or selecting identifiers still takes human time.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
The register tracks materials and custody; individual productivity scoring is outside scope.
Consultation effort under national rules is included where applicable; elapsed procedures may take longer.
unknowns: Whether movement logging already happens directly in the existing system.
Identifier coverage, register quality and the number of physical storage locations.
Available event logs, reporting features and interfaces in the existing system.
Permitted borrower-log retention and applicable employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can configured register features replace custom development?
Which event rules detect duplicate withdrawals, missing returns and conflicting locations?
What capture method works reliably at actual handover points?
new_work: Maintain item labels, locations and borrower references.
Monitor failed captures and reconciliation jobs.
Review report access and remove obsolete borrower data under approved retention rules.

tasks.short: Collect departmental records, check completeness and assemble materials for filing.

steps.what: Check filing schedules and departmental lists to identify materials due.
Request due materials from employees and department administrators.
Collect paper materials from departmental trays and employees.
Download emailed attachments and gather files from departmental folders.
Check required items, identifiers and versions before assembling the filing batch.
Resolve missing, disputed or unclear materials with the responsible employee.

tasks.design: Use the {WORKFLOW} to schedule collection requests and accept records through a structured intake linked to the {DOCS}. Deterministic connectors collect approved digital records and check required identifiers and items against filing checklists. The clerk reviews each assembled batch, collects remaining originals and resolves missing or disputed materials.
tasks.previous_blocker: Departments submitted records through different channels, and filing requirements were often informal.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, scheduled notifications and folder integrations already exist. AI-assisted coding can make the small connectors and validation rules cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Software cannot collect an original from a desk or establish that an unlisted record exists. Distinguishing a final version from a working draft can still require the record owner's explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk knows when a department has supplied the wrong material and can resolve the gap without creating unnecessary duplicate requests.

ambition.what: Filing-readiness checks before internal project closure.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time requesting and downloading records and more time resolving gaps. They can return incomplete batches against agreed checklists; record owners retain responsibility for substantive completeness.

reach.task: Check that project closure records are complete and assigned to an owner.
reach.learn: Closure milestones, document ownership and evidence checklists.

evidence.claim: Scheduled requests, structured submissions and required-field checks need deterministic workflow rather than an autonomous agent.
Rossum checks document-derived orders against rules and routes exceptions, supporting the validation-and-exception pattern.
The cited order-processing capability does not establish automated collection or completeness of departmental archives.

assumptions: Paper collection remains substantial, consistent with the supplied offline-work prior.
A department can define expected record types and required identifiers before automation.
Digital collection is limited to approved submission locations and permitted records.
Step shares and remaining time are estimates; the mix of originals and digital records determines savings.
Access and any consultation required under national rules are included in the build estimate.
unknowns: Which originals must be retained and which can use approved digital submissions.
Whether departmental record lists and final-version conventions are reliable.
Permissions and interfaces available for departmental folders and mail intake.
Who may accept an incomplete batch or change the filing checklist.
research_questions: Which completeness checks can be expressed as explicit rules?
Can direct submission eliminate attachment downloading without moving work onto employees?
Which submission events provide reliable final-version evidence?
new_work: Maintain filing checklists and submission ownership.
Review assembled batches and validation exceptions.
Handle connector failures and unexpected file formats.
Remove duplicate requests and adjust schedules when departments change.

tasks.short: Find requested records, retrieve originals or copies and deliver them to authorized users.

steps.what: Receive and record the request, requester and required delivery date.
Interpret vague descriptions and clarify which records the requester needs.

loop.input: Request text and permitted filing taxonomy.
loop.output: Proposed identifiers, dates, record types and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate fields against the taxonomy; the clerk confirms the interpretation before use.
loop.stop: One extraction and one clarification cycle; unresolved ambiguity returns to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured requests need no model, but informal descriptions can refer indirectly to record types or dates.

steps.what: Search indexes and folders to identify matching records and storage locations.
Retrieve requested paper originals from cabinets or archive storage.
Check requester authority and approve restricted or exceptional disclosure.
Prepare approved copies, checking pages, versions and required exclusions.
Deliver approved records to the authorized requester and record the handover.

tasks.design: Configure request intake and permission-filtered search in the {DOCS}, with the {WORKFLOW} managing exceptional access approvals and delivery logs. A bounded loop proposes search fields for vague requests; configured search and deterministic copy assembly handle the remaining digital work. Approved internal deliveries use controlled links, while the clerk handles originals and checks copy exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent indexing, paper archives and email requests required a clerk to bridge search, permission checks and delivery.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search, access controls and workflow features cover routine retrieval. Small integrations are cheaper to assemble, and a bounded extraction loop can translate informal requests into search fields.
tasks.still_hard: Poor indexing and missing originals limit retrieval regardless of the model. Context-dependent disclosure and redaction require people; permission filtering must protect search results, previews and delivery under GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk distinguishes a plausible match from the correct record and notices when a request could disclose more than intended.

ambition.what: Permission-checked evidence packs for internal project reviews.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching and forwarding routine files and more time resolving uncertain matches and disclosure exceptions. They can curate evidence packs within existing access rights; records owners retain authority to expand access.

reach.task: Assemble source-linked evidence for internal project reviews.
reach.learn: Evidence selection, source traceability and project review requirements.

evidence.claim: Indexed retrieval, access checks and controlled delivery are primarily configured records functions.
TOPdesk Robin answers from maintained knowledge and hands unresolved requests onward; this supports intake and handover, not archive access control.
The digest provides no measured file-retrieval case or guarantee of search accuracy.

assumptions: The target covers internal requests; external disclosure needs a separately defined release process.
Records owners participate in restricted or exceptional requests, rather than every routine retrieval.
Paper retrieval is a branch of the process; fully digital requests skip it.
Routine access follows existing permissions; exceptional access requires records-owner approval.
Copy checks retain time for physical scanning, version uncertainty and required exclusions.
Step shares include records-owner handling and are illustrative workflow effort, not a measured clerk-only time study.
These filing functions do not decide employment, credit or benefit outcomes; EU AI Act assessment follows the actual use.
Build estimates include access work and applicable consultation under national rules; archive cleanup is additional.
unknowns: Index quality, digital coverage and the frequency of vague requests.
Whether search, previews and links enforce the same permissions.
How often retrieval requires redaction, external disclosure or original delivery.
Who owns restricted records and can approve access exceptions.
Whether current interfaces expose reliable versions and delivery events.
research_questions: Can configured metadata search meet retrieval needs before adding a model?
How accurately does the extraction loop preserve identifiers and date ranges?
Do revoked permissions immediately affect search results, previews and existing links?
Which copy exceptions need manual assembly rather than fixed rules?
new_work: Review interpreted requests and uncertain record matches.
Handle denied access, redaction and disclosure exceptions.
Maintain taxonomy, indexing and records-owner assignments.
Test permission boundaries and failed or revoked delivery links.
Monitor extraction failures without retaining unnecessary confidential request text.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward record completeness, custody exceptions and careful disclosure. Routine capture and retrieval shrink, while physical originals and ambiguous cases remain; broader access rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Help administrative services managers prioritise overdue-record recovery.
Help project management specialists prepare complete closure records and review evidence.
Help administrative assistants maintain reusable correspondence templates.
skills_to_grow: Metadata, filing taxonomy and version control.
Rule-based completeness checks and exception handling.
Access control, GDPR-aware disclosure and retention.
Template design and checking bounded model outputs.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a shared records-readiness service that helps departments close projects with complete, traceable files and supplies approved evidence packs for internal reviews.
